target: Il pleuvait sans arrêt pendant nos vacances.
english: It was raining non-stop during our vacation.
tip: 'Sans arrêt' (non-stop) reinforces the ongoing, continuous nature – classic imparfait context.

target: Elle est sortie avec ses collègues vendredi.
english: She went out with her colleagues on Friday.
tip: Sortir uses être: elle est sortie. Agreement with feminine subject.

target: Ils ont joué au football dans le parc.
english: They played football in the park.
tip: 'Jouer' forms passé composé with 'avoir': ils ont joué. Only movement/state-change verbs use 'être'.

target: J'ai poussé la porté et je suis entré.
english: I pushed the door and entered.
tip: Past participle of -ir verbs: finir → fini, choisir → choisi. Regular pattern: drop -r.

target: Tu as répondu à toutes les questions ?
english: Did you answer all the questions?
tip: Répondre to répondu. The past participle of -re verbs ends in -u.

target: Ils sont morts dans un accident de voiture.
english: They died in a car accident.
tip: Mourir uses être: ils sont morts. This is part of the DR MRS VANDERTRAMP verbs.

target: Ils sont arrivés à l'heure pour le rendez-vous.
english: They arrived on time for the appointment.
tip: Past tense with movement/state verbs uses `être`: `je suis allé(e)` (I went). The participle agrees with the subject in gender/number: -e for feminine, -s for plural, -es for both.

target: Il a vérifié les résultats sur son ordinateur.
english: He checked the results on his computer.
tip: Passé composé signals that the checking is finished – he looked at the results and got his answer.

target: Elle a habité à Lyon pendant cinq ans.
english: She lived in Lyon for five years.
tip: Habiter uses avoir in passé composé: elle a habité. No agreement needed.

target: Ils ont construit une cabane dans le jardin.
english: They built a cabin in the garden.
tip: Passé composé tells us the building is complete – the cabin now exists in the garden as a result.

target: J'ai bu un jus d'orange au petit déjeuner.
english: I drank orange juice at breakfast.
tip: Boire to bu. This irregular participle just ends in -u.

target: Elle travaillait dans une librairie à cette époque.
english: She worked in a bookstore at that time.
tip: 'À cette époque' (at that time) sets a past context for describing how things were.

target: Il neigeait dehors et nous restions au chaud.
english: It was snowing outside and we stayed warm.
tip: Weather descriptions in the past use imparfait: il neigeait, il pleuvait, il faisait froid.

target: Ils devaient prendre le train de sept heures.
english: They had to take the seven o'clock train.
tip: Devoir in imparfait expresses past obligation or necessity: ils devaient = they had to.

target: Ils fumaient sur le balcon après le repas.
english: They used to smoke on the balcony after the meal.
tip: 'Quand j'étais enfant' – 'quand' + imparfait sets up a past habitual time frame.

target: Elles ont vu le dernier film de ce réalisateur.
english: They saw this director's latest film.
tip: Voir to vu. Short irregular participle ending in -u.

target: Nous sommes allés à la plage le week-end dernier.
english: We went to the beach last weekend.
tip: Motion/state-change verbs (`aller`, `venir`, `partir`, `mourir`, `naître`, all reflexives) take `être`. The rest take `avoir`.

target: Il pleuvait depuis deux heures quand le soleil est apparu.
english: It had been raining for two hours when the sun appeared.
tip: Imparfait + depuis expresses duration in the past. PC marks when the situation changed.

target: Il faisait beau ce jour-là.
english: The weather was nice that day.
tip: 'Il faisait beau' – weather in the past uses imparfait because it describes a backdrop/state.

target: Je croyais qu'il était médecin.
english: I thought he was a doctor.
tip: Weather in the past uses imparfait: il pleuvait, il faisait beau.

target: Nous avons eu beaucoup de chance.
english: We were very lucky.
tip: 'Avoir' → 'eu' [y]. Very irregular but very frequent. 'Nous avons eu' = we had/got.

target: Nous avons fait de notre mieux.
english: We did our best.
tip: De notre mieux means our best. Faire de son mieux = to do one's best.

target: Tu as fait la vaisselle ?
english: Did you do the dishes?
tip: In passé composé, 'dire' → 'dit': 'Il a dit la vérité' (He told the truth). 'Dire' is for deliberate speech; 'parler' for general talking.

target: Il a pris une décision importante.
english: He made an important decision.
tip: Prendre to pris. The past participle drops -endre and adds -is.

target: Nous avons fait connaissance à une soirée.
english: We met at a party.
tip: Faire connaissance = to get acquainted or to meet for the first time.

target: J'ai fait le ménage dans tout l'appartement.
english: I cleaned the whole apartment.
tip: Faire le menage = to clean the house. Irregular participle: fait.

target: Tu as fait des progrès en français.
english: You have made progress in French.
tip: Faire des progres = to make progress. The participle fait never changes with avoir.

target: Elle chantait sous la douche chaque matin.
english: She sang in the shower every morning.
tip: Repeated actions in the past use imparfait. Chaque matin signals a habit.

target: Je pensais que c'était une bonne idée.
english: I thought it was a good idea.
tip: Mental states in the past use imparfait: je pensais, je croyais, je savais.

target: Il faisait très chaud en été la-bas.
english: It was very hot in summer there.
tip: Imparfait for physical descriptions in the past: 'elle avait les yeux bleus' = she had blue eyes.

target: Il buvait toujours son café sans sucre.
english: He always drank his coffee without sugar.
tip: Boire in imparfait: je buvais, tu buvais, il buvait. Habitual action.

target: Je faisais du vélo tous les matins.
english: I used to ride my bike every morning.
tip: Faire is irregular in imparfait: je faisais, tu faisais, il faisait.

target: Nous attendions le bus sous la pluie.
english: We were waiting for the bus in the rain.
tip: Imparfait describes ongoing actions in the past: nous attendions = we were waiting.

target: Nous avons vu un beau coucher de soleil.
english: We saw a beautiful sunset.
tip: 'Fait' is the past participle of 'faire'. 'J'ai fait mes devoirs' = I did my homework. 'Faire' covers both 'do' and 'make'.

target: Tu as eu le temps de finir ?
english: Did you have time to finish?
tip: Avoir to eu. Very short and irregular past participle.

target: Il a fait ses devoirs avant de sortir.
english: He did his homework before going out.
tip: 'Faire' → 'fait' (done/made). One of the most common irregular past participles.

target: Nous avons fait un gâteau pour son anniversaire.
english: We made a cake for her birthday.
tip: Faire can mean to make or to do. Past participle is always fait.

target: Nous ne comprenions pas pourquoi il était triste.
english: We didn't understand why he was sad.
tip: Imparfait stem comes from the nous form of present tense minus -ons.

target: Tu as mis la lettre dans l'enveloppe ?
english: Did you put the letter in the envelope?
tip: 'Mettre' also means 'to take (time)': 'J'ai mis deux heures' = It took me two hours. Very common usage.

target: Ils avaient un grand jardin derrière la maison.
english: They had a big garden behind the house.
tip: 'Avoir' in imparfait: j'avais, tu avais, il avait. Describes a past state of possession.

target: Nous avons fait le tour de la ville a pied.
english: We walked all around the city.
tip: Faire le tour = to go around. Another common expression with faire.

target: Il y avait un beau parc près de chez nous.
english: There was a beautiful park near our house.
tip: Il y avait (there was or there were) uses imparfait to describe past situations.

target: Nous apprenions l'espagnol au collège.
english: We were learning Spanish in middle school.
tip: Imparfait for age in past narratives: 'elle avait dix ans' = she was ten years old.

target: Ils ont été contents du résultat.
english: They were happy with the result.
tip: Être to ete. This never changes regardless of the subject.

target: J'ai écrit un poème pour ma femme.
english: I wrote a poem for my wife.
tip: 'Avoir eu' = to have had. 'Avoir' is used in many expressions: avoir faim (be hungry), avoir peur (be afraid), avoir raison (be right).

target: J'ai eu envie de partir en voyagé.
english: I felt like taking a trip.
tip: Avoir envie de = to feel like or to want to. Past: j'ai eu envie de.

target: Je lisais quand le téléphone a sonné.
english: I was reading when the phone rang.
tip: Imparfait for the ongoing action (lisais), passé composé for the interruption (a sonné).

target: Tu mangeais quand je t'ai appelé ?
english: Were you eating when I called you?
tip: Question asks about ongoing state when an interruption happened: 'tu mangeais quand je t'ai appelé ?'

target: Je voulais devenir astronaute quand j'étais petit.
english: I wanted to become an astronaut when I was little.
tip: The imparfait expresses wishes and desires in the past: je voulais = I wanted or I used to want.

target: Je ne comprenais pas la leçon de mathematiques.
english: I didn't understand the math lesson.
tip: The imparfait describes how things were – ongoing states, habits, descriptions. Think of it as 'setting the scene' in a story.

target: Ils ne parlaient pas français à la maison.
english: They didn't speak French at home.
tip: After a negation, the article switches: `j'ai un chien` → `je n'ai pas de chien`. The `un/une/des` becomes `de`. Very easy to forget for English speakers.

target: Nous avons écrit nos noms sur la liste.
english: We wrote our names on the list.
tip: Écrire to écrit. The past participle keeps the -t ending.

target: Ils ont vu un arc-en-ciel après la pluie.
english: They saw a rainbow after the rain.
tip: 'Qu'est-ce que tu as fait ?' = What did you do? One of the most common passé composé questions in everyday French.

target: Nous prenions le petit déjeuner sur la terrasse.
english: We used to have breakfast on the terrace.
tip: Habitual past actions use imparfait: nous prenions = we used to take.

target: Nous avions l'habitude de dîner à vingt heures.
english: We used to have dinner at eight PM.
tip: Avoir l'habitude de + infinitive = to be in the habit of. Imparfait for past habits.

target: Nous habitions à la campagne quand j'étais enfant.
english: We lived in the countryside when I was a child.
tip: Imparfait for past states and situations: 'nous habitions' = we were living/we used to live.

target: Il faisait nuit quand nous sommes arrivés à l'hôtel.
english: It was dark when we arrived at the hotel.
tip: With `être`, agreement matters: a woman writes `je suis allée`, men `je suis allé`. Plural feminine `nous sommes allées`. Sounds the same; spelling changes.

target: Nous attendions le bus quand un taxi s'est arrete.
english: We were waiting for the bus when a taxi stopped.
tip: Two actions in the past: ongoing waiting (imparfait) interrupted by a sudden stop (passé composé).

target: Elle pensait à ses vacances quand le patron l'a appelee.
english: She was thinking about her vacation when the boss called her.
tip: Mental states (penser, croire) take imparfait as they describe an ongoing internal state.

target: Ils attendaient depuis une heure quand le médecin est arrivé.
english: They had been waiting for an hour when the doctor arrived.
tip: Imparfait for ongoing background action, passé composé for interruption.
